rated_messages.input_message: Craving a cig? Plan a fun activity you can do when you get home as a reward for not smoking.
Each time you let an urge pass without smoking, you break the old habit a bit more.
Think of your anxious mind like a toddler throwing a tantrum. The best way to respond is to quietly watch, but not give in.

Reduce your stress by using your next break to list four things that have gone well so far today. It might feel like a bit of effort, but doing this will help your mind to refocus, and help you to feel calmer.
Try to stop smoking by setting yourself a rule. For example, "IF I am tempted, THEN I will chew on some mints" - make your own rule that will work for you.
Crumple a piece of paper into a ball and imagine it is your urge. Toss the "urge" into the garbage or against the wall. By doing this, you are letting go of your urges.

Pause. Notice the feelings you are having without judgement. Let them come and go. Being aware of your feelings means you can make a new choice about how you respond to your urges instead of smoking on autopilot.

If you usually smoke while you talk on the phone, try taking the next call in a place where you can't smoke and focus on the conversation. The urge will pass.
Are you willing to let this urge pass for the sake of living a good long time with the people who matter most to you? When you have an urge, think about the people most important to you.
